workExperienceSection.workDescription:
• Rewrote the order gateway's message parser in C++ with zero-copy buffers, cutting median tick-to-trade latency by 18%
• Built a replay tool that feeds a full day of recorded market data through the strategy engine, so every deploy is checked against real trading conditions before it reaches the production servers
• Added per-venue risk limits to the order router, blocking oversized orders in under 2 microseconds with no locks

• Designed a rate limiter in Go for the storage API that keeps any single tenant under its quota across 40 regional clusters
• Moved hot metadata reads to a Redis cache with write-through invalidation, lowering p99 read latency from 45 ms to 9 ms
• Wrote load tests that replay production traffic at five times peak volume, and used them to find and fix a connection pool leak that had been causing weekly outages for two of the largest customers

• Measured how Linux schedules latency-sensitive threads on many-core machines, using tracing tools built with eBPF
• Prototyped a scheduler tweak that pins network threads to idle cores, reducing tail latency by 27% in the lab's benchmark

• Lead a team of six students writing the navigation stack for an autonomous rover in C++ and ROS 2, including path planning, sensor fusion and the simulator the whole team tests with every week
• Set up CI that runs the full simulation suite on every pull request, catching integration bugs before field tests

• Held weekly office hours on threads, memory allocators and networking; answered 600+ forum questions in a semester
• Wrote autograder tests for the malloc assignment that catch heap corruption, used by 900 students each term

projectsSection.projectDescription:
• Price-time priority matching engine handling 4 million orders per second on one core, with lock-free queues
• Python bindings and a backtester that replays historical quotes, used to compare three market-making strategies
• Replicated key-value store on Raft with leader election, log compaction and snapshots, tested with partitions

• Campus navigation app that plans accessible routes between buildings, used by 3,000 students in its first month
• Imports building and elevator data from the university's open data portal and refreshes it automatically every night
